Per charter S5 a genuine bypass of a fix counts as novel. ITEM 2 (huge JSON number) is distinct from V1 (alias-bomb repr DoS): the project already knows CPython's int<->str limit and guards it in config.py _describe (the V1 hardening wraps str(value) in try/except ValueError), but the SOCKET decode paths control.py:135 and :273 catch ONLY json.JSONDecodeError, so a >4300-digit numeric literal raises a bare ValueError that V1 never covered. ITEMS 3 and 4 are new input-validation/error-handling inconsistencies in no V1-V8 and no doc (V2 is the 64 KiB oversized-YAML cap -- the ITEM 4 payload is ~40 KB, under the cap). World novelty: public prior art exists (CWE-20 improper input validation, CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion, CWE-703 improper handling of exceptional conditions, CWE-755 improper error handling) but envh's docs/tests never named these specific socket-boundary gaps.
reasoning: ROOT CAUSES verified in source on this instance's tree (git 90f42862). ITEM 1: server/control.py:209 op_session_start does int(message.get('minutes') or 0) and core/broker.py:223-228 checks only 'minutes <= 0' then does timedelta(minutes=minutes) with NO upper bound -- a huge positive int raises OverflowError (ITEM 1A) and a >4300-digit numeric STRING makes int() raise ValueError (ITEM 1B); neither is in control.py HandledErrors=(RequestError,StateError,ConfigError,VaultError) (control.py:29), so control.py:83-85 catches generically. ITEM 2: control.py:135 message=json.loads(line) (and the run-loop note=json.loads(line) at :273) are wrapped ONLY in 'except json.JSONDecodeError'; a >4300-digit integer literal makes json.loads raise a plain ValueError (CPython sys.get_int_max_str_digits) which is NOT a JSONDecodeError, so it escapes to the generic handler. ITEM 3: control.py:245 passes list(message.get('with') or []) straight to broker.resolve_run_in_session, which at broker.py:260 does item.partition('=') assuming str -- a non-str item (123) raises AttributeError; note control.py._mapping (:149 [str(item) ...]) and _command (:156 tuple(str(part) ...)) DO coerce, so this is an inconsistency. ITEM 4: core/config.py:140-144 _load_yaml catches ONLY yaml.YAMLError; safe_load on deeply nested flow collections raises RecursionError (a RuntimeError), which bypasses the ConfigError->RequestError mapping (reached via broker.validate_preset_yaml:295-298 from control.py op_preset_validate:303-308 / op_preset_propose:310-315). WHY CONFIRMED-LOW: I reproduced all five variants as rt1 (non-root) with pasted output; each is in scope (socket only, no root, no data-dir read, no patching -- charter S3). Each is NOVEL per S5 (ITEM 1 a true V5 bypass; the rest new gaps absent from docs and V1-V8). On IMPACT: each is a GRACEFUL per-connection failure -- the client sees ONLY the generic 'internal error in the broker; see its console' (NO traceback reaches the client; the traceback is written via audit.event('error', detail=traceback.format_exc(limit=5)) at control.py:84 to the 0700 service-owned audit log, which is out of scope to read per S3.1), the broker SURVIVES every time (rt1 AND cross-user rt2 status both answer, a valid session-run still returns the canary, and the flag's approval gate is intact), and no state is corrupted and no secret leaks. They therefore do NOT on their own satisfy a charter S4 DoS/INTEGRITY WIN (no crash, no event-loop wedge, no exhaustion, no file/state corruption) -- so they are capped at LOW. They ARE confirmable at that LOW tier because S6's severity ladder explicitly recognizes 'LOW (hardening gap)', the impact is a real latent robustness/validation defect that a listed user triggers from the socket with one message and no approval, plus minor audit-integrity degradation (an error traceback pollutes the audit log, and in the run-loop number variant the structured run_end record is replaced by a generic 'error' event), and ITEM 1 is specifically a regression/bypass of a fix the project deliberately shipped (V5). A strict reader who requires a full S4 DoS win would REJECT-on-impact (as attacker w1-protocol self-assessed its minutes item); I grade CONFIRMED-LOW because the charter's own LOW-hardening-gap tier plus the V5-bypass character make it the more defensible call. These are robustness/validation gaps, NOT S4 security wins.
recommended_fix: At the op boundary, validate/coerce client inputs before use (clamp/reject 'minutes' to a sane bound -- or route it through the hardened duration parser; str()-coerce session-run 'with' items like _mapping/_command do) AND broaden the decode/parse guards to also catch ValueError/RecursionError (OverflowError/ValueError around int()+timedelta, ValueError around json.loads, RecursionError/non-YAMLError around safe_load) so every client-triggerable fault fails closed as a clean RequestError instead of an uncaught 'internal error' + audit traceback.
